# Dwellir Examples

> Curated code examples, demos, and AI agent skills for blockchain development.
> Organization: dwellir-public (https://github.com/dwellir-public)
> Website: https://www.dwellir.com
> Last updated: 2026-10-30

## How to use this file

This file is an index of all public Dwellir example repositories. Each entry is a self-contained project you can clone and run. Some examples live as folders inside this repository under examples/. For structured data, see examples.json in this same repository.

To get a Dwellir API key (required by most examples): https://www.dwellir.com

---

## Code Examples

### gRPC Code Examples
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/gRPC-code-examples
- Chain: Multi-chain
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Beginner
- What it does: Connect to Dwellir's gRPC service and stream blockchain data. Getting-started examples for the gRPC API.

### Hyperliquid Orderbook Server Examples
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/hyperliquid-orderbook-server-code-examples
- Chain: Hyperliquid
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Beginner to Intermediate
- What it does: Progressive WebSocket examples — from basic connections to L2/L4 orderbook data to calculating market metrics (VWAP, spreads, volume). Six examples that build on each other:
  1. WebSocket basics — connect and subscribe to BTC trades
  2. L2 orderbook — aggregated orderbook with spread visualization
  3. Multiple subscriptions — handle multiple coins and data types
  4. L4 orderbook — track individual orders
  5. Reconnection handling — robust client with auto-reconnect
  6. Data analysis — VWAP, spreads, volume calculations

### Hyperliquid Builder Codes Demo
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/hyperliquid-builder-codes-demo
- Chain: Hyperliquid
- Language: TypeScript (Next.js)
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- What it does: Interactive web app for Hyperliquid builder codes. Approve builder codes, trade with builder fees, and revoke. Wallet-connected frontend.

### x402 Payment Protocol Demo
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/x402-demo
- Chain: Base
- Language: TypeScript
- Difficulty: Beginner
- What it does: Minimal demo of the x402 protocol — HTTP-native micropayments using USDC. A joke API that costs $0.001 per request. Server returns HTTP 402, client pays, request goes through. Three interaction modes: Express server, browser frontend (MetaMask/Rabby), and headless client for bots/agents.

### Base Flashblocks Visualizer
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/example-base-flashblocks
- Chain: Base
- Language: TypeScript (Next.js)
- Difficulty: Beginner
- What it does: Side-by-side visualization comparing 200ms flashblock pre-confirmations vs 2-second standard block finality. Polls the same Dwellir endpoint with "pending" (flashblocks) and "latest" (standard) block tags. Shows real-time transaction counts, gas usage, and a speed multiplier. Includes a transaction race feature to track individual transactions through both detection methods. One React component, raw JSON-RPC, no external libraries.

### Robinhood Chain Rust Trading Bot
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/robinhood-rust-trading-bot
- Chain: Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain ID 4663)
- Language: Rust
- Difficulty: Beginner
- What it does: 54-line bot using ureq + serde_json. Every 2 seconds it calls eth_blockNumber and eth_call slot0() on the WETH/USDG 0.01% pool (0x52e65b17fb6e5ba00ed806f37afcd2daa50271ca), converts sqrtPriceX96 to a USD price, and paper-trades a 5-vs-20 moving-average crossover starting from $1,000. Read-only; never signs transactions. Endpoint comes from the DWELLIR_URL environment variable. Includes a timestamped video transcript (TRANSCRIPT.md).

### Arbitrum Rust Trading Bot
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/arbitrum-rust-trading-bot
- Chain: Arbitrum mainnet (chain ID 42161)
- Language: Rust
- Difficulty: Beginner
- What it does: Same 54-line bot as the Robinhood example (ureq + serde_json), pointed at the WETH/USDC 0.05% pool (0xc6962004f452be9203591991d15f6b388e09e8d0). Reads slot0() every 2 seconds, converts sqrtPriceX96 to a USD price, and paper-trades a 5-vs-20 moving-average crossover from $1,000. Read-only. Endpoint from DWELLIR_URL. Includes TRANSCRIPT.md.

### Hyperliquid ABCI Snapshot to L4
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/hyperliquid-abci-snapshot-to-l4
- Chain: Hyperliquid mainnet
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- What it does: Reads a periodic_abci_states/<date>/<height>.rmp (or .rmp.lz4) snapshot with plain msgpack and writes every resting order on every perp, spot and outcome market as L4 JSON in the same [coin, [bids, asks]] shape as hl-node compute-l4-snapshots, with every hl-node field including the TP/SL children and trigger fields. Use it when hl-node fails on an older snapshot with "missing field ...", because Hyperliquid only publishes the latest hl-node and the state format changes at some upgrades. Includes compare_l4.py, which checks the output against an hl-node export; on block 1145900000 all 492,491 orders and 7,554 child orders match. Needs about 20 GB RAM.

### Hyperliquid Wallet Data in Go
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/hyperliquid-wallet-data-go
- Chain: Hyperliquid mainnet
- Language: Go
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- What it does: Four programs for a list of your own wallets (WALLETS in .env). wallet-events streams funding payments and ledger updates (deposit, withdraw, send, spotTransfer, internalTransfer, vault and staking moves) from gRPC StreamMiscEvents with a users filter, filters the hourly Funding deltas on the client (one event lists every position, tens of MB; 256 MB receive limit), and resumes from the last cursor with progress frames; replay reaches about 2 days back. fills-history pages userFillsByTime on the Dwellir Index (2,000 fills per page, history since 2025-07-27, billed per fill) and dedups by (tid, oid). hip3-markets uses perpDexs, meta/clearinghouseState/openOrders with "dex": "xyz", gRPC StreamBbo and StreamAllFills with dexes. builder-staking reads maxBuilderFee (tenths of a basis point), delegatorSummary and delegations. The README lists the Info request types the Dwellir endpoint does not serve (userFills, userFunding, userNonFundingLedgerUpdates, HIP-3 metaAndAssetCtxs, delegatorRewards) and the alternative for each. Generated gRPC code is included.

### Hyperliquid gRPC Machine Learning
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/hyperliquid-grpc-ml
- Chain: Hyperliquid mainnet (HyperCore)
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- What it does: Replays recent fills from Dwellir's Hyperliquid gRPC StreamFills feed (about 96 hours of replay on 2026-10-25; replay then live tail on one call) and rolls taker fills into 1-minute bars with signed flow, opening flow (from each fill's dir), and liquidation notional. mlkit.py has causal building blocks in numpy and pandas: rolling statistics, forward labels a model cannot see early, recursive least squares with forgetting and ridge, forecast scoring (IC, hit rate, Newey-West t, one-bar delay), a Kalman filter for a drifting hedge ratio, PCA, and walk-forward PCA regression. hl_index.py and collect_bars.py --source index|candles build the same bars from the Hyperliquid Index: allFillsByTime fills with liquidations joined from liquidationFillsByTime, or 1s/1m/5m OHLCV candle ranges and dashboard full-history exports, back to 2025-07-27 (bars from Index fills matched gRPC bars exactly on 2026-10-28). Candle bars have no taker side, so research.py switches to price inputs. research.py runs all of them on the bars; live.py warms the online model on replayed history and keeps it learning on live fills. Needs a Dwellir API key; the gRPC paths also need the Hyperliquid gRPC add-on.

### Hyperliquid Trade Post-Mortem
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/hyperliquid-trade-postmortem
- Chain: Hyperliquid mainnet (HyperCore perps, including HIP-3)
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- What it does: Pages one wallet's fills from userFillsByTime on the Dwellir Hyperliquid Index (2,000 per page, cursor time_txIndex, billed per fill) and rebuilds round-trip trades from each fill's startPosition; fills in one block are ordered by txIndex, not tid. Loads 1s candles for each trade's entry and exit minute and 1m candles to 24 hours after the exit from /v1/candles/range, cached on disk. Measures MFE, MAE, capture and the move 1, 4 and 24 hours after the exit. simulate() replays the real entries and exits bar by bar under a rule (stop, take, trailing stop, max hours, no adds, stop then re-enter on a bounce), using the wallet's own fee rate plus 5 bps slippage on stops, and 1s candles to break ties when a stop and target share a minute. Each trade gets one of six lessons (skip, stop, take, hold, reenter, no_adds) or fine. test_rules() scores every rule on the earlier and later half of trades separately. postmortem.py prints the report; postmortem.ipynb adds charts. A 30-day run on a 1,118-fill wallet used about 44,000 API credits. PnL excludes funding.

### Hyperliquid Vaults and Leaderboard
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/hyperliquid-vaults-leaderboard
- Chain: Hyperliquid mainnet (HyperCore)
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Beginner
- What it does: Ranks every open Hyperliquid vault by TVL, APR or day/week/month/all-time PnL from the stats-data vaults feed (9,478 vaults, 3,062 open, about 14 MB, cached on disk), inspects one vault with the public vaultDetails query (leader, fees, window returns, largest followers, child vaults for HLP) plus its live positions from Dwellir clearinghouseState, and lists the vaults an address leads with leadingVaults (needs user; returns 422 without it). Ranks the 48,192 traders in the stats-data leaderboard feed by PnL, ROI or volume per window with min account value and min volume filters, keeps only vault leaders when asked, and profiles the top N in one Dwellir-only batchClearinghouseStates call (billed per wallet). Shows a wallet's vault deposits, APR and lockups with userVaultEquities. vaultSummaries returns [] and vaultDetails/portfolio are not on the Dwellir proxy, so hl_api.py routes those two to the public Info endpoint.

### Multichain ERC-20 Transfers
- Path: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-examples/tree/main/examples/multichain-erc20-transfers
- Chain: Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum One, Polygon PoS (mainnets)
- Language: Python
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- What it does: Pulls one address's ERC-20 Transfer logs with plain eth_getLogs, address in topics[1] for sent and topics[2] for received, keeps 3-topic logs (ERC-721 shares the signature with a 4th topic), merges both directions on (tx_hash, log_index) with self-transfers marked once, and sorts by block and log index. Self-sizing windows condensed from the eth_getLogs limits guide: reads the plan cap and the suggested range from rejections and halves on a timeout. decimals() and symbol() via eth_call, cached, bytes32 symbols handled, exact amounts by integer arithmetic. Marks rows above the finalized block; reorg_check.py re-reads their block hashes and exits 1 on a replaced block. native.py finds native and internal transfers with trace_filter (Ethereum, Base; 100 blocks per call), debug_traceBlockByNumber callTracer (Arbitrum; one call per block), or LogTransfer logs from the POL system contract 0x...1010 on Polygon (matched every traced POL value transfer, internal included, in a test block). Measured 13 Nov 2026 on Dwellir: 10,000-block eth_getLogs range on all four on a 10,000-block plan; result cap 20,000 logs on Ethereum and 10,000 on Base; none at 84,116 logs on Arbitrum or 130,333 on Polygon.

## AI Agent Skills

Skills are structured knowledge files that give AI coding agents deep context about blockchain APIs. Install with `npx skills add`.

### Dwellir Skill (140+ chains)
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/dwellir-skill
- Install: npx skills add dwellir-public/dwellir-skill
- Scope: 140+ blockchain networks
- What it enables: EVM JSON-RPC, Substrate/Polkadot (@polkadot/api), non-EVM chains (Aptos, Sui, TON, TRON, Starknet), trace/debug APIs, WebSocket subscriptions, Hyperliquid gRPC streaming. Four sub-skills: dwellir (hub), evm, substrate, hyperliquid.

### Hyperliquid Skills
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/hyperliquid-skills
- Install: npx skills add dwellir-public/hyperliquid-skills
- Scope: Hyperliquid L1
- What it enables: HyperEVM JSON-RPC, Info API proxy, gRPC streaming, Orderbook WebSocket, trading patterns, dedicated nodes.

---

## Developer Tools

### Skills Benchmark
- Repo: https://github.com/dwellir-public/skills-benchmark
- Language: Shell
- What it does: Sandboxed benchmark harness for measuring how infrastructure skills affect AI coding agent performance. Run controlled experiments comparing agent output with and without skills loaded.

---

## Common patterns across examples

- All examples follow: clone → install → add API key → run
- Python examples use pip + requirements.txt
- Rust examples use cargo (cargo run --release)
- Go examples use go run ./cmd/<name>
- TypeScript examples use npm/pnpm + package.json
- API keys come from https://www.dwellir.com
- Each repo has its own README with full setup instructions
